matter_reference_date_basis: exam_session 'OCTOBER 2022' recorded in candidates/matters/M043.json. The latest event in the scenario is Rikitha's death on 02.08.2016, so every provision relied on must be in force by October 2022 and, for each devolution, at the relevant date of death.
corpus_gaps: No provision in the corpus states the effect of a deed of gift that conveys the dominium absolutely and irrevocably while reserving life interests to the donor and a third party, or the extinction of such a life interest on the life tenant's death. That is Roman-Dutch common law, reached through s.36 of the Ordinance but not itself in the corpus, and it is what makes Nihal's 2003 intestacy pass nothing in Lot 5.

The Partition Law No. 21 of 1977 is not in the corpus, so the conclusiveness of the final decree in Partition Case No. 516/P as the root of Nihal Gamage's title cannot be supported from a corpus provision.

Section 25 of the Ordinance says that the full siblings and the qualifying half-siblings take the other half but does not say in what proportions among themselves. The draft resolves this by s.30, per capita, all being equally near in degree; s.27 supplies a competing proportional rule and s.36 sends the residue to Roman-Dutch law. No corpus provision decides which controls.

Whether Anusha, the mother of Nikitha and Rikitha, survived Rikitha's death on 02.08.2016 is not stated. This is an open scenario fact rather than a corpus gap, but it selects between s.25 and ss.26-27 for Rikitha's estate and the verifier must resolve it.

Nothing was found in the corpus on the succession consequences of a testamentary case being terminated, as District Court of Kaduwela Case No. 1052/2006/T was on 27.11.2007. Civil Procedure Code s.526 is recorded as background only.

enrichment.original_background: By a Final Decree dated 07.09.1999 entered in the Partition Case bearing No. 516/P of the District Court of Kaduwela, all that allotment land marked Lot 5 depicted in Partition Plan No. 1100 dated 06.05.1997 made by W.P. Gunaratne Licensed Surveyor of the land called Delgahawatta bearing Assessment No. 3A, Sarasavi Lane situated at Battaramulla 30 perches in extent was allotted to one Nihal Gamage. The said Nihal Gamage upon Deed of Gift No. 663 dated 21.11.2002 attested by Athula De Silva Notary Public of Colombo, gifted the said Lot 5 in the said Plan No.1100 unto his son, Piyal Gamage as an absolute and irrevocable gift subject to the life interests of the Donor and his wife Kanthi Gamage. Thereafter, Nihal Gamage died intestate on 28.04.2003 leaving as his intestate legal heirs his wife Kanthi Gamage, his 3 children by their marriage, namely, Piyal, Aruna, Leela and 2 children by his previous marriage to Anusha, namely Nikitha and Rikitha. Piyal Gamage died intestate on 02.08.2006 unmarried and issueless and his estate was administered and letters of Administration was issued to his mother Kanthi Gamage in the District Court of Kaduwela Case No.1052/2006/T. The proceedings were terminated on 27.11.2007. Kanthi Gamage met with an accident and died intestate on 17.03.2010. Rikitha married to Sanatha and died intestate on 02.08.2016 without having children.

gold_answer_draft.issue: The pedigree has to trace Lot 5 from Nihal Gamage, who took it under the final decree in Partition Case No. 516/P, through Deed of Gift No. 663 and then through three successive intestacies - Piyal in 2006, Kanthi in 2010 and Rikitha in 2016 - to the persons who hold the land today. The questions are what Nihal was left with after the gift, who took Piyal's dominium, who took Kanthi's share once her life interest fell in, and who took Rikitha's share.
gold_answer_draft.rule: Inheritance ab intestato to immovable property in Sri Lanka is governed by Part III of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, s.21(1), which applies to the estate of anyone dying after its proclamation, s.20. Subject to the surviving spouse's one-half under s.22, the order of succession is descendants, then ascendants, then collaterals, s.23. Children are preferent to all others and take equally per capita, with the issue of a deceased child taking per stirpes, s.24. Where descendants fail and only one parent survives, that parent takes half and the other half goes to the full brothers and sisters and to the half-brothers and sisters related to the intestate through the deceased parent, s.25; those siblings being equally near in degree take that half per capita, s.30. Where both parents fail, the estate goes to the brothers and sisters, whole or half-blood, s.26, and where the half-blood is on one side only the full siblings take the first half and share the remaining half with the half-blood, s.27. 'Unmarried' means not having a husband or wife living, s.3, so no s.22 share arises out of the estate of a person who dies unmarried. Where the Ordinance is silent the Roman-Dutch law of North Holland governs, s.36; that is the source of the rules on a donation reserving a life interest, which the statutes do not address.
gold_answer_draft.application: The final decree of 07.09.1999 vested Lot 5 in Nihal Gamage. By Deed of Gift No. 663 of 21.11.2002 he gifted the lot to his son Piyal absolutely and irrevocably, reserving life interests to himself and to his wife Kanthi. The dominium therefore passed to Piyal in 2002; what Nihal kept was a life interest, which is not an inheritable interest and fell in on his death on 28.04.2003. Nihal's intestacy in 2003 accordingly passes nothing in Lot 5, and his heirs take in this land only through the later intestacies. Kanthi's life interest continued after 2003 and burdened Piyal's dominium. Piyal died intestate on 02.08.2006 unmarried and issueless. Having no spouse (s.3, s.22) and no descendants (s.24), s.25 applies: his father Nihal had predeceased him, his mother Kanthi survived, so Kanthi takes half of the dominium and the other half goes to his full sisters Aruna and Leela and to his paternal half-sisters Nikitha and Rikitha, who are related to him through the deceased parent, in equal per capita shares under s.30. The letters of administration issued to Kanthi in District Court of Kaduwela Case No. 1052/2006/T, terminated on 27.11.2007, administered that estate but did not alter the devolution, Civil Procedure Code s.526. Kanthi died intestate on 17.03.2010; her life interest was extinguished on that date and the land became unencumbered, and the half she had inherited from Piyal passed under s.24 to her surviving children Aruna and Leela, Piyal having died before her without issue to represent him. Nikitha and Rikitha are not Kanthi's children and take nothing out of her estate. Rikitha married Sanatha and died intestate on 02.08.2016 without children. Her husband takes one-half of her share under s.22. The background does not say that Anusha survived; proceeding on the footing that neither parent survived Rikitha, the other half of her share goes under s.26 to her sister Nikitha and her paternal half-sisters Aruna and Leela, divided in the s.27 proportions because the half-blood is on the father's side only: Nikitha takes the first half of that collateral portion and shares the remainder with Aruna and Leela.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The pedigree runs: Nihal Gamage under the final decree of 07.09.1999; Deed of Gift No. 663 of 21.11.2002 to Piyal Gamage subject to the life interests of Nihal and Kanthi, so that Nihal's death on 28.04.2003 carried nothing in Lot 5; Piyal's intestate death on 02.08.2006 dividing his dominium as to one-half to his mother Kanthi and one-half equally among Aruna, Leela, Nikitha and Rikitha; Kanthi's intestate death on 17.03.2010 extinguishing her life interest and passing her half equally to Aruna and Leela; and Rikitha's intestate death on 02.08.2016 passing one-half of her share to her husband Sanatha and the other half to Nikitha, Aruna and Leela. The present owners are therefore Aruna, Leela, Nikitha and Sanatha. Two points remain open: whether Anusha survived Rikitha, and whether the sibling half under s.25 is divided per capita under s.30 or in the s.27 proportions.

answer_claims.claim_text: Intestate succession to Lot 5, being immovable property in Sri Lanka, is governed by Part III of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, which applies to the estate of any person dying after its proclamation.
Subject to the surviving spouse's one-half, the right of inheritance devolves in the order descendants, ascendants, collaterals.
Where the Ordinance is silent on a question of distribution, the Roman-Dutch law of North Holland governs; the corpus contains no provision on the effect of a donation reserving a life interest.

Under Deed of Gift No. 663 the dominium of Lot 5 passed to Piyal Gamage in 2002 and Nihal retained only a life interest, so Nihal's intestate death on 28.04.2003 devolved no interest in Lot 5 on his heirs.
Piyal died unmarried within the meaning of the Ordinance and left no descendants, so neither the surviving spouse's half nor the preferential right of children arises out of his estate.
Where descendants fail and only one parent survives, the surviving parent takes half and the full siblings together with the half-siblings related through the deceased parent take the other half.
Siblings who are all equally near in degree to the intestate take per capita and not per stirpes.
On Piyal's death Kanthi took one-half of his dominium as surviving parent, and Aruna, Leela, Nikitha and Rikitha took the other half in equal per capita shares.
The grant of letters of administration to Kanthi in the testamentary case did not alter who succeeded to Piyal's estate.
Children are preferent to all others in the estate of a parent and take equally per capita, the issue of a deceased child taking by representation.

On Kanthi's death her life interest was extinguished and the half she had inherited from Piyal passed equally to her surviving children Aruna and Leela, Piyal having predeceased her without issue and Nikitha and Rikitha not being her children.
A surviving spouse inherits one-half of the property of a person dying intestate, so Sanatha took one-half of Rikitha's share.

Both parents failing, the estate goes to the brothers and sisters of the whole or half-blood, and where the half-blood is on one side only the full siblings take the first half and share the remainder with the half-blood.

On the footing that neither of Rikitha's parents survived her, the other half of her share passed to her full sister Nikitha and her paternal half-sisters Aruna and Leela in the proportions fixed by section 27.
The pedigree therefore ends with Aruna, Leela, Nikitha and Sanatha as the present owners of Lot 5, the land being free of both reserved life interests since 17.03.2010.

gold_answer_draft.issue: What fraction of Lot 5, 30 perches in extent, is presently owned by each heir, given that Nihal parted with the dominium by Deed of Gift No. 663 in 2002 and that Piyal, Kanthi and Rikitha each died intestate thereafter.
gold_answer_draft.rule: The same Part III rules govern each computation. Inheritance to immovable property in Sri Lanka is regulated by the Ordinance, s.21(1), for estates of persons dying after its proclamation, s.20. A surviving spouse takes one-half, s.22; 'unmarried' means not having a husband or wife living, s.3. Subject to that half the order is descendants, ascendants, collaterals, s.23. Children take equally per capita, issue of a deceased child by representation, s.24. Descendants failing and one parent surviving, that parent takes half and the full siblings and the half-siblings related through the deceased parent take the other half, s.25, which they take per capita being equally near in degree, s.30. Both parents failing, the siblings of whole and half-blood take, s.26; the half-blood being on one side only, the full siblings take the first half and divide the remainder with the half-blood, s.27. Where the Ordinance is silent the Roman-Dutch law of North Holland applies, s.36, which is what governs the reserved life interests.
gold_answer_draft.application: Take the whole of Lot 5 as 1. Piyal held the entire dominium from 21.11.2002, subject to the life interests. On his death on 02.08.2006 without spouse or descendants (s.3, s.22, s.24), s.25 gives Kanthi as surviving parent 1/2, and the remaining 1/2 is shared per capita under s.30 by Aruna, Leela, Nikitha and Rikitha, so each of the four takes 1/8. On Kanthi's death on 17.03.2010 her life interest ended and her 1/2 passed under s.24 to her surviving children Aruna and Leela, 1/4 each; Nikitha and Rikitha take nothing out of her estate. Holdings then stood at Aruna 3/8, Leela 3/8, Nikitha 1/8 and Rikitha 1/8. On Rikitha's death on 02.08.2016 her husband Sanatha took 1/2 of her 1/8, that is 1/16, under s.22. On the footing that neither of her parents survived her, the other 1/16 passed under s.26 to her full sister Nikitha and her paternal half-sisters Aruna and Leela, divided under s.27: Nikitha takes the first half of it, 1/32, and the remaining 1/32 is divided among Nikitha, Aruna and Leela, 1/96 each. Nikitha therefore adds 1/32 plus 1/96, which is 1/24, and Aruna and Leela add 1/96 each.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: On the reading adopted, Aruna owns 37/96, Leela owns 37/96, Nikitha owns 1/6 or 16/96, and Sanatha owns 1/16 or 6/96, of Lot 5; the four fractions total 96/96. Against the 30 perch extent that is 11.5625 perches each to Aruna and Leela, 5 perches to Nikitha and 1.875 perches to Sanatha, and the land is free of both life interests since 17.03.2010. Two alternatives must be resolved before these figures are treated as settled: if the sibling half of Piyal's estate is divided in the section 27 proportions rather than per capita under section 30, every figure changes; and if Anusha survived Rikitha, section 25 applies to Rikitha's estate and Anusha takes 1/32 with Nikitha, Aruna and Leela taking 1/96 each.

The background never says whether Anusha, the mother of Nikitha and Rikitha, survived Rikitha's death on 02.08.2016; the draft proceeds on the footing that she did not, which engages section 26 and section 27. If Anusha survived, section 25 applies to Rikitha's estate instead and Anusha takes 1/32 of the land, with Nikitha, Aruna and Leela taking 1/96 each. The construction point is how the sibling half under section 25 is divided among full and paternal half-siblings: the draft applies section 30 per capita; on the competing reading section 27 proportions apply to that half, which would give Aruna and Leela 3/16 each and Nikitha and Rikitha 1/16 each out of Piyal's estate and change every downstream figure. A lawyer should settle both before this is treated as gold.
